answer: At the XL scale, the byte-level H-Nets cross over the tokenized Transformer after 200B bytes for H-Net (space), 100B bytes for H-Net (1-stage), and 30B bytes for H-Net (2-stage) [Dynamic Chunking for End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Modeling, arXiv:2507.07955v2, PDF p. 12, §3.1 Language Modeling]. After these crossover points, the performance advantage of the H-Nets widens progressively [Dynamic Chunking for End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Modeling, arXiv:2507.07955v2, PDF p. 12, §3.1 Language Modeling].
question: At the XL scale, the byte-level H-Nets start behind the tokenized Transformer. After how many training bytes does each one cross over, and what happens to the gap after that?
raw_answer: At the XL scale, the byte-level H-Nets cross over the tokenized Transformer after 200B bytes for H-Net (space), 100B bytes for H-Net (1-stage), and 30B bytes for H-Net (2-stage) [[cite:9c6bbf025fbc1469]]. After these crossover points, the performance advantage of the H-Nets widens progressively [[cite:9c6bbf025fbc1469]].
